acceptancePoints.text: Embedded review metadata is deterministic and identifies the exact build channel, revision, feature commits, source thread, and issue.
The review section appears in personal Dev and Test builds and does not appear in Release or ordinary Debug builds.
Each review item shows the problem, reproduction steps, change summary, checks, expected success, validation, limits, and attribution without trimmed text.
An item with fresh proof pending explains that state and cannot submit a Ready for Dev verdict.
Ready and Not ready require confirmation and preserve the exact build and feature identity in the queued verdict.

features.behavior: Show the exact contents and evidence of personal Dev and Test builds, and require a confirmed verdict for the exact feature and build before stream promotion.
features.knownLimitations: Installing a build does not approve any item. SwiftUI Dev and upstream remain unchanged until the explicit human gates are completed. Commit 11658353d7175c55ab745c469f0c8861c1448db5 also strengthens the theme accessibility test, so this staged item and the theme item share that rollback dependency.
features.name: Review features and visualize their PR promotion pipeline
features.problem: The phone had no exact-build review queue. A person could not tell which commits and source threads were installed, see their proof, or send an auditable verdict without leaving the app.
reproductionSteps: Open Settings in SwiftUI Test and open What’s testing.
Expand a review item and inspect its guidance, proof, commits, source thread, and issue.
Choose a verdict and inspect the confirmation before canceling or submitting it.
features.successLooksLike: The priority order is clear and every required section is readable without trimmed text. A pending-proof item explains its state and cannot be approved. A review-ready item expands working clean and annotated links. The diagram shows candidate PR → Test build → your Test approval → Dev build → your upstream approval → upstream PR. Test preserves exact build evidence before queuing a verdict.
features.summary: Adds an in-app review queue for exact Dev and Test build contents, plus a phone-readable diagram of the proposed PR-based path from a proved candidate through Test, Dev, and upstream.
features.validationSummary: Exact Test source dae630726 passed 414 native tests across 43 suites, the 130-test XCTest aggregate (129 passed, 1 skipped), and all 25 UI journeys. Fifteen schema-v2 proof packets are sealed, and the review-readiness gate reports 15 items with zero errors.
features.whatToCheck: In Test, open Settings → What’s testing. Confirm items are ordered by priority and show their review group. Expand this item and verify Original problem, numbered Steps to reproduce, What changed, What to check, Success looks like, Automated validation, and Known limits. If the app says fresh proof is being recorded, confirm Ready for Dev is disabled and wait for the replacement packet. When Visual evidence appears, verify its links, commits, thread, issue, confirmation dialog, and both readiness choices.

acceptancePoints.text: Newer live messages and working state win over stale initial history.
A message or status does not disappear, duplicate, or revert when the initial history response arrives.

features.behavior: Merge initial thread history with newer live events so the first history response cannot erase, duplicate, or revert messages and working state that arrived during opening.
features.knownLimitations: A useful manual check needs a thread with a live update during the initial history request.
features.name: Preserve live updates during initial thread open
features.problem: A slower initial history response can replace a newer live event, so a message or status can appear and then disappear or revert during first open.
reproductionSteps: Choose a thread that is receiving a response or another live update.
Open the thread while its stored history is still loading.
Watch the newest message and status through the first load, then leave and reopen.
features.successLooksLike: Messages and status move forward without briefly appearing and then disappearing, duplicating, reverting, or requiring a manual refresh.
features.summary: Prevents the first thread-history response from overwriting newer live messages or status updates that arrive while the thread is opening.

acceptancePoints.text: The SwiftUI Home header no longer carries the development build badge, leaving its controls and swipe space clear.
Settings About shows the exact development build, revision, upstream ahead/behind distance, and commit link with a complete accessibility label.

features.behavior: Keep the Home header uncluttered and place exact development-build identity, upstream distance, and commit navigation in Settings About.
features.knownLimitations: The row is intentionally limited to development configurations. Ahead/behind values reflect the metadata embedded by the build pipeline; the public Release app remains unchanged.
features.name: Move SwiftUI debug build identity and base distance into Settings
features.problem: The old development badge occupied scarce Home-header space while showing only partial build identity. It competed with navigation and swipe controls and did not explain how far the build was from Theo's SwiftUI base.
reproductionSteps: Open a personal SwiftUI build and inspect the Home header beside its navigation and action controls.
Open Settings and scroll to About.
Read the Development build row and inspect its commit-link affordance and accessibility description.
features.sourceThreadTitle: SwiftUI pipeline stability and PR #5789 shipment
features.successLooksLike: Home has no development badge. Settings About shows build 60, the exact bbbf98df revision, 461 commits ahead and 0 behind Theo's SwiftUI branch, exposes the commit link, and announces the full identity accessibly.
features.summary: Removes the compact debug badge from Home and adds a dedicated Development build row in Settings About with full revision, upstream distance, commit navigation, and accessibility metadata.
features.validationSummary: Exact aggregate proof commit bbbf98dffbaa4c088cc4dfc4044e14b519aabc75 passed 416 focused native tests in 43 suites and all 4 PR-level UI journeys. The feature's five focused metadata tests also passed. Dark-mode Simulator evidence and accessibility inspection confirmed build 60, the full revision, and 461 ahead / 0 behind.

acceptancePoints.text: The personal Test app is compiled with Swift optimization and whole-module compilation, strips build products, and does not load the Xcode debug dylib.
DEBUG fixtures, T3_PERSONAL_BUILD behavior, and testability remain available in the optimized Test configuration while Dev remains debuggable.
After a cold launch reaches Home, the populated list accepts its first drag and visibly moves without a dead interaction period.

features.behavior: Compile only the personal Test channel as an optimized, directly linked executable so a restored launch snapshot is not left visible while a large debug image finishes loading.
features.knownLimitations: The optimization is intentionally limited to the personal Test configuration. Dev remains unoptimized for debugging, and the final cold-launch judgment still requires the physical phone build with real Test data.
features.name: Make Test builds interactive immediately after cold launch
features.problem: The personal Test channel shipped an unoptimized debug image and could display its saved Home snapshot while the app was still loading, making the visible interface appear unresponsive for several seconds.
reproductionSteps: Force-quit SwiftUI Test.
Cold-launch SwiftUI Test and immediately swipe the Home list or tap Settings.
Confirm the first input responds without waiting several seconds.
features.summary: Builds the personal Test channel with optimized Swift and direct executable linking while retaining its DEBUG fixtures and testability.
features.successLooksLike: SwiftUI Test accepts its first Home scroll or Settings tap immediately after a cold launch while all Test-only features and fixtures continue to work.
features.validationSummary: The frozen integrated commit passed 416 native tests across 43 suites and four Candidate journeys. The final optimized Test configuration separately passed 33 FeatureRootModel tests and the focused cold-boot Home journey; the built app contained no debug dylib and accepted its first recorded Home drag.
features.whatToCheck: Cold-launch SwiftUI Test and immediately scroll Home or tap Settings. The first input should respond without the previous several-second dead period.
